tips.comment: Zgharta finished second last time out in a Class 2 over a mile at the course. The horse was only beaten by half a length and was staying on.

Pearla is an interesting runner here, with Haggas' horses normally getting an easy introduction. But given the fact that she has an Irish Oaks entry, this horse could be something special. Worth a bet at these odds.
The stable is coming into form and does well with debutants. It has ability in its breeding and should go well on debut.

UNDERSTUDY catches the eye here for a yard in red-hot form. John Gosden's runners have been performing well of late, and he has a good 23.08% strike rate at Newmarket in 2025. Oisin Murphy's booking catches the eye, and I have high hopes for this horse in this contest.

Potentially my only play on Friday comes in the form of ALPINE TRAIL. Aurel has to be taken seriously given his winning debut at Kempton last year, however this is a marked step up in class and trip plus we have no idea if he’ll be fully fit on reappearance. Ernst Blofeld took came forward from his debut LTO, winning at Kempton when stepped up to 10f, however that was a lowly C5 novice event and I wasn’t entirely convinced. Nebras will do well to overcome H Doyle’s 2% SR (A/E 0.4) on unfancied runners in 3yo races and R Moore’s uncharacteristic 3% SR (A/E 0.42) on outsiders at HQ puts a line through Harvey. AT looks a favourite who should win by default as well as on merit and 5/4 can be taken. The son of Dubawi overcame plenty of greenness to win at Wolvo on debut before showing a much more polished display at Yarmouth last month. You’d expect a further step forward here given the breeding + connections, he’s got a top + blue FlatStats rating and Dubawi’s 65% SR (A/E 1.51) with French-born favourites adds further confidence. C Appleby has also won 4/9 renewals.
This horse is very well-bred, and as you would expect, it has a very good set of figures against its name. So, in a small field, I suspect it could do well.

The weather here in Newmarket has been almost unbearably hot this week. My pet Greyhound, Sky, and I walk the Newmarket racecourse almost daily, but we have not been down there since last Sunday. My point? It will have been a fantastic effort by the ground staff if the going is good today. It will be at least good to firm. One bet for me: the Gosden-trained Ernst Blofeld.

Cosmic Year won by 6.5 lengths on debut at Sandown last September and returned from a break to win by 5 lengths at Kempton last month. He looks a top prospect, and with Ryan Moore booked to ride, he can take this Listed Race.

Symbol Of Honour heads to Newmarket in good nick after a couple of sharp wins in Dubai. Steps back up to 7f which should suit fine and he’s already shown he handles the track. With Buick back on, he looks a solid player in this Listed race.
Marvelman is available at big prices for a yard that is going very well at the start of the season. All of these are open to big improvement, and I think this looks like great value.
Beat Irish 2000 Guineas entry Anno Domini by half a length over course and distance last month and likely to come on for that run which was on the back of a 173 day break,
Being aimed for Royal Ascot. Not sure what he beat last time, but he did it by more than 6L, so has to be taken seriously. Upped in class here but has an each-way chance.

Was Superb winning here over C&D last September, but up in trip also here LTO halted that progress when only 7 of 9 last month. But can bounce back strongly, which is also helped by dropping down in class.

2:20 @ Newmarket - Port Light 22/1. On balance, I thought Port Light could be in the overpriced category. His 3rd at Chelmsford was won in a pretty quick time where he set the pace over a mile. He was a bit too free, but if allowed to freewheel over shorter, he could spring a bit of a surprise here and prove an interesting contender up the rising ground if he can get some of these uncomfortable early. He’ll have some company up front, likely in the shape of the Waco Kid. So, providing husband and wife don’t cut each other's throats, I think they could both prove interesting to catch. With Marquand's mount saddling a penalty, preference for me is an each-way play on this improving sort.
Buick on board and has some very impressive form from last year. Makes handicap debut today and should be hard to beat.
Needed run on reappearance. Makes handicap debut after 3 runs. Improved from debut to 2nd run last year, and Spencer has been booked for this.

FORT GEORGE represents a leading owner and this trainer and jockey have both made solid starts to the new season including at this venue. Not too many ride Newmmarket better than Tom Marquand and seen for the first time as a three year old this handicap debutante appeals.

Dantes Lad has been gelded since he won a C4 after a break in November. Although up 5 lbs for that, this step up in class to C3 puts him still well-weighted among today's runners, with Billy still in the saddle, who was on top for that last win.

Wild Nature steps into a hot-looking mile handicap at Newmarket off a mark of 90. He looked useful when breaking his maiden at Kempton and has scope to improve, but he’s now 2lb worse off with Dante’s Lad who beat him earlier. Still unexposed so he’s not one to rule out.

Big Sip is a promising three-year-old competing in a Class 3 handicap over a mile, with the winner set to receive nearly £21,000. After an impressive victory in the Lingfield maiden in March, some concerns arose from his subsequent performances. He struggled on his handicap debut and was disappointing on soft ground at York. However, those underwhelming outings can be attributed to unfavorable conditions. Now, returned to a more suitable fast ground and having been dropped to a mark of 85, Big Sip is expected to perform significantly better this season, especially against competitors making their seasonal debuts.
Interesting booking for Moore with this one. Having form recently and after a break, had a nice pipe opener last time out and could go close today.

Progressive 4-year-old well suited to 7f on good ground. Strong seasonal return, ideally drawn, and tactically versatile. Tom Clover does well with older handicappers, and Neil Callan is a smart booking. Likely to sit handy or lead, and outstay his rivals with a turn of foot.

The racing surface is expected to be on the faster side, with some water potentially being applied to ensure optimal conditions. Track bias is a consideration at Newmarket, warranting observation. The betting focuses on the 3:30 handicap race, a class 2 event for four-year-olds and older, featuring a substantial prize of over £25,000 for the winner. The horse called Miss Information is anticipated to perform well following her recent seasonal reappearance, as trained by Andrew Balding, who possesses a notably large and promising roster of horses. Despite a lackluster market presence upon her return, Miss Information is believed to have benefited from that outing. With a career record of three wins from thirteen on turf and previous successes on fast ground, her experience and recent performance suggest a strong showing is likely at an attractive price in this competitive race.

This is the value bet running off a mark 2lb below his last winning mark last August and is a previous course and distance winner. Decent reappearance run on penultimate start, first home in his group, and can be forgiven his run last time. Fit and prepped to go.

Jumby returns to Newmarket where he’s a course-and-distance winner and has gone well in top-end handicaps. He wasn’t far off in a strong race here last time and with Buick back on, he’s got every chance of getting seriously involved off a workable mark.
Has won 3 and placed in 3 of 9 starts on the all-weather but has not been as good in 2 turf starts. Each way chance if bringing all-weather form here.
Charlie Appleby and William Buick team up at Newmarket and could have a few winners, including Silver Knott, who has had his last 11 races abroad. Only 4 runners here, but it's a race full of class.

Entitled to improve for his 2nd start of the season and for his new stable. Form tailed off last year but his peak efforts are clear in this field including 2nd in The Derby and 3rd in the Irish Derby.
Divina Grace returned from a break last month, running for a new yard, and came straight in with a G3 win. She could improve again now, second up in this G2, while keeping DP in the saddle.
Rosy Affair has hit the crossbar a few times and returns off a mark of 88 after three runner-up finishes. Buick’s back on and she’s been holding her form well, so another bold bid looks likely.

Ran well to finish fourth over 7f at Doncaster in March when returning from almost six months off and wasn't beaten far when finishing second over the same trip at Redcar eleven days ago. Ryan Moore in good form recently. Should be thereabouts.

Not a deep-looking class 3 to close out this Newmarket card, and I'd like to see the Gemma Tutty-trained Ormolulu get away on level terms for a change. If he does, he must have a great each-way shout with an eye-catching booking of Rossa Ryan.

Well-deserved win at Chelmsford back in January of this year. However, easily outclassed LTO when only 11 of 12 at Lingfield back in February of this year. But now, mark eased and drop down in class represents good value.

The only 3 year old in the field and gets a handy weight allowance from the rest of the field. She is trying this trip for the first time and a previous winner over 7 furlongs. Weakened over 7 furlongs here last time out but will come on for that run with the drop back to 6 furlongs of interest.

Turned into a bit of a CD specialist and ran another good race on the 15th when 3.25L behind More Thunder when giving him the best part of a stone. Looked to be traveling in to win that there but faded back to 3rd. Possibly needed the run and would come on for that anyway. However, we know she loves the GF ground and that was Good To Soft. Has previously been a NR on that surface and if improving for the better ground she should definitely be fav and hard to believe she's available at 11/2 considering she re-opposes More Thunder with everything in favor. Likely to be prominent and kick on, and if so, will take all the catching.
Went third towards the finish despite being denied a clear run approaching the final furlong over 7 furlongs here last month. Remains on the same mark but drops in trip, which could suit.

Something amiss last year, just four runs but he was a close runner-up on his final start. The 4yo ran well for a long way on his return three weeks ago, after a 7 month break, showing a high cruising speed from the front over 8f, tired late on. He ran well at Group level as a 2yo. On a decent mark, he can be better for the return run and if he gets a soft lead in this 6f handicap he might be hard to catch.
I think he is listed/G3 class and did well to win at Royal Ascot despite a bad draw and running wide. Race conditions are ideal. Should go well.

The 5yo is an interesting runner in this handicap. He ran to a decent level in the English and Irish 2000 Guineas as a 3yo. He raced in Australia last year - average form. Big run on his return to the UK five weeks ago, only beaten 2L in the £77K 22 runner Lincoln handicap, staying on well at the finish. Should be better for the run and the extra furlong should help.

Unlike most of his rivals in this race, Son Of Sarabi has already made his debut and was only a neck behind in that debut race at Doncaster, finishing 2nd and showing excellent speed. There is a chance of a win in this race

Several of these have more experience than this horse and that may give those others an advantage so this is risky but, newcomers from this yard often run well first time out, including at this course. This horse has a decent pedigree and starts off over an ideal distance.

Sands of Mali colt, a half-brother to the impressive 5f winner Storm Call. His dam, a maiden who raced up to 1m, is a half-sister to the talented winner Electrelane, who excelled at distances up to 1m. With trainer Andrew Balding boasting a commendable 18% win rate and the in-form Jason Watson set to ride this promising 2-year-old, he certainly warrants an each-way bet at 20/1.
Improved on a debut 2nd place with a win at Brighton last month. Carries a penalty in a tougher race but with improvement likely, holds every chance of following up.
Noble Champion finished very quickly in the Greenham, which looks pretty decent form now and stretching out to a mile looks like it will be the making of this horse.

Secret Theory was hooded when he won first time out at Newmarket, then won again 189 days later when stepped up to a mile. More to come from this colt by Dubawi. First time ride for Jim Cowley, who will hold him up from stall 4.
Ran consistently in 5 races last year, winning once and finishing 2nd once. Started this year with another 2nd place finish, and with further improvement still likely, could go 1 better.
The outsider of the field of 6, but not without a chance this afternoon. Won its debut race and ran okay last time out when 3rd, so could spring a surprise win at decent enough odds.
Won over course and distance last season. Comes here 3lb higher than for his last win in September, his penultimate start, and had excuses for his poor last time as he was turned out too quickly.

Has the potential for a soft lead here, and whilst he needed the run in 2024, he did win fresh in 2023, so the break becomes less of a worry. His reappearance run in 2024 was on GS ground, his only run with soft in the going barring a 15 of 16, so perhaps that’s a feasible excuse. He progressed last season, which included an all-the-way win here, and with Dods having a good day at Ayr yesterday, he is also 4/7 here in the last 5 years. With the horse 2 from 2 on undulating tracks, and 3 from 3 on sharp tracks, this setup could just be ideal.

Only 2-12 but a talented individual who was group placed at 2 and picked up a first handicap win at Windsor last summer. Really solid 2nd at HQ on reappearance a fortnight ago and any kind of step forward from that should make this son of Bated Breath hard to beat today.

A 5-time career sprint winner who won 3 times last year, the last 2 both came in Class 2 handicaps at Ascot. Finished 6th at Southwell last month on seasonal return when looking in need of the run. Should come on for that run and looks sure to run well today.

Has been running consistently on the all-weather this year with 2 wins from the last 5 starts. Carries a 3lb rise for the latest run now switched to turf, but on current form holds an each-way chance.
RPR top-rated and won first time out last season. Won at Listed level in September in a good race at the York August meeting.

Weighted to beat Shaha, 3lb better off for a half-length beating last year. Improved when stepped up to this trip on his last run of the year, storming away from a Class 2 field, so deserves the chance up in grade.

An interesting Listed event for the fillies, and a chance taken on the battle-hardened and improving Allonsy. She has 10 lbs to find with Scenic, so this could well be a stretch too far. But whilst the latter won fresh last year, it was by far her worst effort of the season, so she could be in need of this. The drop in trip is a plus for this horse who did well over further last time, suggesting if she can get a nice forward position and potentially lead (she looks one of a couple of pace angles), she could dictate the pace and fall down the hill late on and stay there. She may be better off taking a lead from Our Golden One in the hope she falls into some laps late on.
From a good family, and this step up in trip will suit her. The ground beat her when last seen in a Listed race in France back in November. Worth an each-way bet on this ground and trip.
3 lengths behind the re-opposing runner-up Fifty Nifty over course and distance 16 days ago but 4 pounds better off in the official ratings and could reverse that form on these terms.
Our Golden One takes a shot at Listed company at Goodwood after some solid runs in handicaps. She stays well and has good course form, so while she needs to step up, she’s not out of it entirely.

Lightly raced 4yo filly. She improved in the second half of last year, posting three good RPR ratings despite not winning. Her 2L defeat in a 14 runner Listed contest last Sept - quick ground - is solid form. Improvement very possible after her 6 month break from the track and can play a big part in this Listed race.
Panthera has stuck to racing on the continent for a lot of last year and now drops into listed class. Not many really have this pedigree, so this looks a good each way bet.
Waleefy returns from a break after a solid 3yo campaign that included two wins and a good third at Ascot. Up to a mark of 88 now but still unexposed and could pick up where he left off.
Kept on when 5th of 19 but 2nd in group when the field split over this trip at Doncaster last time out. Drops a pound and could be fired up by the first time blinkers.

Race 5 at Goodwood today is the Elston Supports UK Financial Advisers Handicap (Class 3) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,207 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 8-year-old gelding Spring Bloom from the Robert Edderry yard, and will be ridden by Mason Paetel. This son of Power is a 6-time winner and has a handy 3.2 kg apprentice allowance from jockey Paetel as an extra advantage. Sure to run well considering his recent consistency.
Looks on an enticingly low mark now with the jockey claiming 7 lbs. Has gone well here before, and the jockey and trainer teamed up for a winner recently. Can hit the frame on these terms.
Handicap debut for Andrew Balding. On his last run, he looked like he wanted a step up in trip, and the stable does very well with handicap debutants.
Has been gelded since 2-year-old races. If he's trained on as a 3-year-old, he will improve enough to take part in the finish, as the trainer is in good form. So if ready, ducks in a row, in the mix.

This horse was held up and staying on well when upped to around this trip last time out, which was his seasonal debut run. He looks primed to run a big race here now that he'll strip fitter. The horse's sire produces some decent sorts (he's produced several Group winners), and the horses close to this one in class 2 and class 3 novice races last year provide enough clues to suggest Bentbasa could be on a decent mark of 73 here.

This horse has yet to win but has run well in defeat on many occasions, has shown quite a consistent level of form. Ran well on the AW when last seen, probably a better horse on turf so this could be more suitable than last time. Open to some improvement
Magna Gee Gee stayed very strongly off the front at Chelmsford last time out, which is a feat in itself, and at these odds with 4 places on offer, should be able to go very close here.

Has seemingly taken to obstacles well, and in the last race at Fontwell, he beat a 110-rated horse. Now returning to the flat, if you were to translate this rating to this code, this horse should go close.

An Alan King trained 4-year-old who has had 6 races on the flat, winning twice. His last win was in August last year in a class 5 handicap at Newmarket over 1m 2f on good going, ridden by today's jockey David Egan, when leading 1 furlong out, staying on at the finish to win by 2 lengths. He is in a class 4 handicap over 1m 6f on good going. This gelding finished 2nd of 12 runners 17 days ago at Kempton in the a/w in a class 5 handicap over 1m 4f when staying on at the finish, beaten 1/2 a length by the favorite. He has had the benefit of having a recent race, he is upped in class and in distance. Has an e/w shout in this race today.

Has run a couple of decent 3rds here in the past, both over 2m. Good 3rd when last seen in November and comes here on a 5lb lower mark than his last turf outing. Has gone well fresh in the past and might not be far away with in-form Sean Levey on board. Drop back in trip could suit.

Junkanoo represents the Gary & Josh Moore stable. He has a record of 4 wins. The stable has good stats in this race as well as a good performance in the last 2 weeks. Junkanoo has been 3rd in his last 2 races. He starts today with a mark of 75, and has a win in his career with a mark of 80. The chances of a podium finish are pretty strong

Open looking race, i wouldn't be surprised to see Currumbin at least run better than what these odds suggest, was running well on the AW when last in action , he's still fairly unexposed on turf so it's difficult to rule out some improvement at some point. First run back from a rest but he's not been away from the track for too long, still worth considering. Drawn well , good jockey booked.
All-weather form is better than form on the turf but arrives having won at Wolverhampton last time. Each way chance if in the same form on this surface.

Was fairly impressed by the seasonal debut run in the Listed AW race. First step up to the mile and powered home to be beaten by a nose by Soprano. Would have won that the stride after, and would she be 9/2 had she downed a dual G1 placed and Royal Ascot winner on the first run at 1m? Bound to come on for the run for the Gosdens, and it's possible that Wathnan have a good one on their hands here. Won at Ascot on Good and Firm in the US. Has race fitness and experience advantage over some of these, and at 9/2 I'll take the chance that she follows up with another big run. 1m+ favors those held up.

Moreton's dam is from a classy family, and the pedigree box is being ticked in a start. Add to that a debut third last month at Yarmouth behind a couple of experienced runners. I am tipping Moreton's can take on the odds-on favorite Meelaf, and he can come out on top in this Maiden Stakes.

Moulin Booj returns to turf at Musselburgh today after a couple of solid efforts on the all-weather. Back over 5f in a Class 4, he’s got a decent draw and a mark he can work with so should have a good chance.

Mehmas gelding who packs plenty of punch and potential and is best not judged on his most recent outing at Pontefract 24 days ago where finishing 8th/10 as that was his return run after a 171 day break and he did shape like in need of the outing however this race is a whole different scenario that represents a drop back down from class 2 to class 4 company and B Haslam's inmate arrives here fit from a run and in top nick currently operating on a very attractive mark of 79 Wen Moon looks poised to strike here and he has been competitive of higher marks than this worth noting he is now operating 5lb below his last winning mark jockey P Mulrennan takes the ride and can give Wen Moon the perfect ride here at Musselburgh must be considered of this sort of mark

Protest Rally has so far, shown his best form at Class 5 and Class 6 level so will need improvement in this Class 4 race but, some improvement is possible because as a 5yo, it's difficult to rule out some further progress and his previous form at this course is encouraging.

I'm chancing Abduction here at Musselburgh, he hung badly right when he was last seen here on the 13th April. So I'm hoping something was just amiss that day as he is a better horse than that. He's dropped down 9st 4lbs for tomorrow's run and Lauren Young claims a very handy 7lbs as well. Let's hope he bounces back.

A 7-time career sprint winner who was rated as high as 103 back in 2023. Form regressed last year, though not disgraced in competitive sprints. Looked in need of the run when 6th over 5f at Southwell on seasonal return last month. Showed plenty of early speed to lead but failed to last home, weakening in the final furlong. Dropped another 3 lbs to a very handy mark of 80 and should strip fitter today. Could take some catching down to Class 4.

At the bottom third of the handicap mark and had a race to forget last time out when 12 of 12 here over C&D. But she can bounce back, and it helps she's a three-time C&D winner and now just 1 lb above the last winning mark.

A beaten favourite in an amateur race over 2 miles here on the 2nd of April and runner-up when joint favourite when last seen 7 days later over 2 miles and 2 furlongs at Pontefract. Could be suited by this drop in trip.

This Irish mare won twice in a row around Musselburgh last October and has finished second and third since at Musselburgh and more recently Pontefract. Back down in trip and I am tipping Reel Her In will catch the rest to win this six runner handicap.

Ran well to win over C&D last month when returning from six months off beating reopposing Coconut Bay by a neck but finished just outside the places in fifth over the same trip at Catterick a week later. Is a two time C&D winner. Should be thereabouts.
There was a neck between this one and Doomsday when they last met over c/d. But I think the selection can reverse the placings, and the jockey's 3lbs claim should come in very handy for this rematch.

This horse has looked back in some better form on her last 3 runs which were on the All-Weather surface, she acts well on turf so has a chance and she did run well in 2 of her last 3 runs at this course. Current rating is fair so she can't be completely overlooked in my view.

RAMON DI LORIA gets in cheaply after the win last time out and the step up in grade shouldn't be an issue as he was very competitive when last seen in that company. Looks a bit of a tasty price all things considered.

Returned with a solid run in Class 4 company and now drops into a Class 5, nearly a 10lb ease in opposition. Runs off 71, having won off 72 last season (over a mile). His third-last run showed enough to justify favouritism next time at Newmarket, though he disappointed there. Back down to 7f now, which could suit if ridden prominently. Has the form to go close at this level. Good luck!
Capital Guarantee squeaks into this class and is about to be raised in the handicap too - so should in theory be in tougher company than this. Can double up here.

Just one win from 16 runs is not good, but she looks to be moving in the right direction after an encouraging run last time out at Catterick last month when she was 3rd of 9. She can build on that effort despite the mark being unchanged this time out.

A 9lb rise isn't enough to stop this horse, with trip and ground all exactly the same as for his two previous wins. Joe Fanning is back on board, so it will be another positive ride, and he should bring up the hat trick as this race is weak. He's been well placed by Julie Camacho, whose horses are flying at around a 25% strike rate for the last two weeks, including a winner last night.

The market revolves around the 2/5 favorite here (Two B Tanned) with punters diving in for her to land the hat trick after two easy wins. They were both at Beverley, and the first of those she was sent off at 25/1. She's 12lb higher now, so I can't help thinking that her chances have been exaggerated here. This second favorite looks to be the one to step up should the favorite falter. He won on his only previous run over C&D off the same mark, and it looks significant that he's reunited with the same jockey after several runs without him on the AW. Looks great value to me at 9/2 and is the best value of the day for me.

Speedy 3-year-old with rapidly improving form and a profile suited to sharp 5f. Drawn well, capable of early dominance, and has proven finishing kick. Trainer/jockey combination is in good form. Has a clear edge in pace and class, making her a strong contender in this modest sprint.
Fairly Famous has strong rivals today. However, his wins in this race in the two previous years and good current form suggest a winning attitude. Chances of winning look high.
Won 1 of 11 starts for previous yard and was a winner of a point last month on first start for this yard. Holds an each-way chance if finding best form.

Fourth in the Hunter Chase at Cheltenham over this trip and running on at the end, so no problem on the trip. Missed Aintree, so will be fresher than Gracchus De Balme, who is not guaranteed to see this trip out. Between these two.

Consistent stayer with proven ability over long distances on good ground. Shows stamina and race fitness, with excellent amateur jockey booking. Stable has strong record in similar events. Expected to sit close to pace and grind it out late. Well-weighted and tactically solid against weak competition.

Having been pulled up in a handicap chase at Stratford 7 months ago with Joe Tickle, this 8-year-old showed potential by finishing 3rd in a restricted point in March. With a fresh trainer and a jockey who can claim 7lb, the 28/1 odds could offer a valuable choice for an each-way bet.

Last win on a professional track was back in December 2023, when taking two wins on the bounce at Hereford. Has changed yards since and comes here on the back of a couple of successful run-outs at longer trips. Does seem prepped for this race and should handle the four-mile distance.

Kelly Morgan's Go Go Geronimo has been regularly running in hunter chases this season and has been placed three times. He was out of his depth in the Aintree Foxhunters last time, but this represents a more suitable opposition and he has a chance here.

Myth Buster is at his best at this sort of marathon trip on good ground. Returning from a 70-day break, he was 2nd 26 days ago in a 4m1f point on good, which showed him to be in good heart. He should be fitter today, and the 12-year-old has run this course well (under today's rider) over a shorter 3m2f, staying on well in May 2023.

Won at Fontwell in May last year but disappointed in two races since and was pulled up on two point starts since joining this yard. Needs to rediscover last year's form, but that would give an each-way chance.

Finished 2nd in Foxhunters at Aintree over 21f on good to soft 29 days ago and should go close again. Has never run here at Cheltenham but has winning form from 19-26f, so the tough uphill finish shouldn't hold any worries and is also ground versatile if any heavy rogue showers happen.
Not beaten that far in Grade One at Aintree when last seen. If handling the drop back in trip, should prove better class than these.
Won this race last year and showed he’s still capable by narrowly winning at Newbury six weeks ago. He’s tough and reliable at this level and clearly goes well at Cheltenham.

Cap Du Mathan was second at Ludlow latest over a similar distance. He looks well treated on past form and this represents a drop in grade. His trainer does very well over the season in fox hunter events.

Billy Bathgate will go well but has only won one in forty-one races. The selection needs to bounce back from some poor runs towards the end of last season, but that might happen having had a wind operation during the break. The stable is going okay.
Ran a decent debut at Newbury and is upped in trip. Looks to be progressive. Top yard that is going well at the moment. Former apprentice champion jockey on board.

National Park returns to Newcastle tonight after a promising debut fourth at Kempton last month. He showed good early speed and kept on well, suggesting he’ll come on for the run. With that experience and a favourable draw, he looks a strong contender.
National Park is interesting with a run behind that one. But this Butler horse is highly thought of at home and will be well prepared for debut. Good alternative. Is bred for this surface.
Chuzzlewit has flopped down the handicap, despite being a tidy horse. Hoping that this is the moment to catch this horse, and off a low mark, has got a great opportunity.

SAVVY KINGDOM could of course go one of two ways following his eye catching seasonal reappearance. If building on that effort then as a four year old he could prove a well treated racer and he has an often favoured high draw which is to his advantage.
Took the eye on his comeback run recently and has fallen down to a nice mark. Top jockey booked and interesting to see the money come.
Improved with each run on the flat, the most recent of which suggests that this opening handicap mark is going to be more than workable for him.

Leadman has been knocking on the door with four second-place finishes from seven starts, including a close second at Kempton last October. Now off a mark of 83, he’s got a solid chance to finally get his head in front.

Benacre hasn't won since a 2-year-old, with form being slightly patchy since then. Showed up better at Musselburgh 2 races ago, losing by a neck, but didn't perform at the same course a week later. Is capable of bouncing back today.

Was a class 5 C/D winner 4 starts back and followed that up with a good effort also over C/D at this level when beaten less than 2L carrying 9st 5lb. Coming from well back with a storming late run. Carries 8st 13lb today, its lowest so far, which may well see it bag its first AW class 4 today. Is the top speed-rated horse in the lineup.
Not so good last time out, but will be a different proposition this evening at its favorite track, Newcastle. Twice a C/D winner and rarely finishes out of the frame here.
Bobby Joe Leg has been quiet the last couple of runs but drops back into a winnable race off a mark he’s scored from before. Wouldn’t be a surprise to see him bounce back.

MAKEEN runs with the yard in fine recent form , so the lack of a recent run may not be an issue. Indeed he has won when fresh albeit some time ago now , but he does have the assistance of a 5lb claiming apprentice aboard and now down as low as Class 6 handicap company he should be competitive.
Harry Magnus is a good each way chance here in this field and just couldn't land a blow off the pace at Wetherby. Newcastle is better suited to this run style and this represents a good chance here.

Gained more valuable experience over C&D LTO last October despite only finishing 11th of 12. But at least last win off a higher mark and has a 3lb claimer this time out. So with some improvements, should be in the mix.

Damisa makes his handicap debut at Newcastle after a year off and drops into a weak Class 6 off just 46. He didn’t show much as a juvenile but the break, gelding, and new trip could all spark improvement. Wouldn’t be a total shock if he outran his odds.
Course and Distance specialist winning 5 times here and although not been in front since February is running respectably in defeat. A good opportunity here to get back to winning ways.

A moderate sprint handicap where Athollblair Boy can bounce back from a poor run last time on the turf. Now he switches back to the all-weather. He was just touched off here over the same distance previous to that, and off of the same sort of mark, should go close. 9/1 looks big.

Blackcurrent was a very close second here back in February off today's mark. While not so good for the last three runs off the same mark, I think the change of rider today claiming 3 lbs might get him back in the game.
Flavius Titus did win off today's mark when here in August. While I would have preferred a rider with some wins under their belt, Kyle is claiming 5 lbs and could be worth an EW 4P.

Low draws are favored here, and another race is likely to be run at quite a pace. The run in the Lincoln can be ignored due to being hampered at a crucial stage. The time before, on the AW Lincoln trial, looked as good as ever when running on well to be nearest the finish. Only run on good or better three times, including 2nd in Maiden. 2nd 3.75L behind Jayarbee in a listed race last year over 1m2f, then didn't stay the 1m2f on the 'rain-softened ground' next time. Back to 1m on a quick surface should suit and will be rattling home. The form behind Jayarbee is very solid for a race of this level, and it's possible the ground will see him back to that standard.

The 5yo is an interesting runner, 16 career runs and is now making his handicap debut. He has spent his time running in Listed and Group races and has been rated 113, now running off a 102 mark. Decent run three weeks ago on his return in a useful looking conditions race.

Just failed in the Hunter Chase at Cheltenham, staying on really well up the hill. Won this last year after a 2nd at Cheltenham and a win at Aintree, so should be fresher this year (gave Aintree a miss). A very consistent performer.

Has beaten Its On The Line and now looks a bit of value. Had two poor runs after but looked likely to bounce back after third at Down Royal and did so next time at Fairyhouse, winning. Might well add to that win here.

Was mightily impressive in last hunter's chase victory when making all and winning by over 20 lengths. Should be at least placing at worst and represents value against a horse that's got a poor beaten favorite record and is expensive to follow.

Although I am keen on Ontheropes, I am sweeter on this horse who ran a fine race at 100/1 at Cheltenham when sixth in a big field. A repeat of that should be good enough to get the horse in the frame.
Dinoblue won the Mares' Chase at Cheltenham by 8 lengths, beating all of her main rivals here. That was her 7th win over fences, and she looks likely to add another today.

Dino Blue is a short-priced favourite and brings the best recent form into the race, having won comfortably at the Cheltenham Festival, beating several of today’s rivals. However, at around 4/1, Allegorie De Vassy makes plenty of appeal returning to a right-handed track, having jumped to her right before falling last time out. She’s a classy mare on her day and was only narrowly beaten by Dino Blue at Naas, finishing just a neck behind. She looked impressive when scoring at Fairyhouse in January, and a repeat of that performance would bring her right into contention. Receiving 6lb from her main rival, the weight swing could make things very interesting.

It's all gone wrong recently for Constitution Hill after falling at Cheltenham and at Aintree, and without doubt, it knocked his confidence. Still, he was travelling okay in both races before making uncharacteristic jumping errors. He can put everything back on track today with a good performance at Punchestown.

I didn't think I would say this, but Constitution Hill just can't be trusted. State Man looks the obvious alternative after being so unlucky in the Champions Hurdle. Back on home turf, he could make amends for that final flight tumble at Cheltenham.
The two market leaders look too short here and so for some better value I am going to back Golden Ace who is on the back of 2 good wins and will be fresh from a break.

2nd in the Turners Novice Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival in a tight finish but lost nothing in defeat. Can gain some compensation today in better-suited ground and can go close for trainer Gordon Elliott.

This is a cracking renewal, and it looks like it could be fought out between Final Demand and The Yellow Clay. Final Demand was 5 lengths behind The Yellow Clay at Cheltenham, but he was eased off near the finish when beaten, so had an easier race, which could give him the edge here. He should also be suited by the slightly softer ground and the right-handed track, as he was so impressive at the right-handed Limerick on his first outing under rules.

At extreme odds, it feels rude not to have a small each-way bet on Belloccio at around 25/1. He may have something to find on official ratings, but he has looked progressive over hurdles and brings solid staying credentials from the Flat, including a win over a long trip at Royal Ascot, where he is now rated 105. A dual-purpose performer for Willie Mullins, he finished like a rocket last time out to snatch third in a Grade 2 at Fairyhouse, suggesting there is more to come. Already a course winner here at Punchestown, he stayed on strongly that day, and the booking of Rachael Blackmore adds further appeal. With the drying ground in his favour, he could easily outrun his odds.

A proven flat winner who made an impressive return to hurdling after a four-month break, landing a competitive 8-runner Grade 2 contest at Fairyhouse (20f) just 26 days ago. The addition of cheekpieces appeared to sharpen him up, as he showed a smart turn of foot to quicken and snatch victory near the line. Stepping into deeper waters here, but his upward trajectory suggests he's not out of place, and he looks capable of making his presence felt. With jockey J.J. Slevin in flying form and enjoying a strong Punchestown Festival so far, confidence in the saddle could be a key asset.

The model is suggesting an upset here, but we have to take it at face value after recently predicting a 51/1 winner, Buy Some Time, and a 22/1 winner, Transprint, recently. Tripoli Flyer steps out here with a relatively high RPR compared to the other runners, but without an official ranking. Both The Yellow Clay and Final Demand look like formidable horses at the top of the market, so maybe the each way play is a better risk-return here. I don't typically like Each Way, but at 17s, the value and price are big enough to justify. Three places up for grabs in the 9-runner field.
Fountain House has 7 wins on his record, including 6 wins in PTP races. His 2nd place in this race last year (odds of 33/1 then) could well change to 1st today, barring any surprises
Ran well on debut to win comfortably over 3m at Cork eleven days ago. Should improve further today. Jockey's 5lb claim should come in useful. Should be thereabouts.
Asphalt Cowboy has come in the top three in his last four races, winning his last race at Downpatrick. I think he has a good chance of challenging for 1st.

Although this horse was beaten fair and square by Fountain House in February here at Punchestown, the addition of cheekpieces could help turn the form around. The connections won this race last year. This horse was a beaten favorite at Tramore but wasn't beaten far. Runs well here.

King Rasko Grey was only fourth in a big money bumper on debut in April last year but returns today in a race that is a bit more doable, with a yard that will have him ready for this return in calmer waters.
Mondouiboy came second in his last two races. He races today in this flat race at Punchestown. With some heavy competition, he has shown he can place with his recent form.
Point winner who finished a good 2nd at Newcastle on bumper debut in February. Should appreciate this longer trip and holds an each-way chance at least.

This twice-raced maiden has already defied expectations by finishing 2nd at Clonmel. Much will hinge on his adaptation to the shorter distance, but the jockey's 7lb claim allowance could ease the load. At 40/1, this is an incredible value bet.

The model I run suggests Runcok can win this one. Steps out with the highest RPR of the field by quite a long way and doesn't seem to be overly punished in the weights. Other horses carrying lesser weight have significantly lower ratings. Paul Townend picks up the reins, who's in excellent form and rides for Willie Mullins' yard. Runcok is a prior course and distance winner, so looks like the play here.

Raced freely third in a novice hurdle at Windsor. Most recent run giving far too much to do. That form franked at Graded and Listed level. Returning from a break, multiple French bumper winner. Very interesting with improvement likely.

Looks the wrong price for me after a couple of strong efforts, winning a Grade 3 juvenile before finishing 4th in a Grade 2 behind some of the leading Irish 4-year-olds. Fell at Aintree last time but should appreciate the quick ground here for his yard that does so well with these types. Brings graded form to the table in this novice hurdle and, in receipt of the 4-year-old weight allowance, should be the one to beat.

Blizzard Of Oz won two of his 4 starts over hurdles and has finished 3rd in all three starts over fences, finishing close up in each. This looks a fair mark for his handicap debut, and he looks a good each way bet. 5 places on offer.
Jumped very well when winning by a wide margin last time. This is a much tougher race, up in grade, and she goes up 8 lb, but is very much worth an each-way bet for 5 places.

Sean Bowen is a positive jockey booking and although the blip was his run at the Cheltenham festival he has shown good form, winning at Cheltenham on trials day in January and finishing a respectable 4th when last seen in listed company. A good opportunity here at a nice price with places on offer to make a profit on the each way terms.
Nara has been brought to life by fences and looks a high-quality mare that can only improve. I'm surprised this horse isn't nearer favouritism here. Good each-way chance.

Comes into this off the back a decent run lto. Dropping back slightly in trip. With a 5lbs claiming jockey booked to ride. She's yet to scale the same heights she reached over hurdles in 5 chase runs. Her best RPR over hey does was 145. Where as her best RPR over fences is just 134. Her chase win at Fairyhouse reads well. She beat her 2 stable mates Karia Des Blaises and Paggane comfortably. That form looks better now with the 3rd winning nto. Then subsequently going close behind stable mate Fun Fun Fun in a listed race. She's a classy horse on her day. She won a Grade 1 as a juvenile. She also finished a close 3rd behind Lossiemouth in the Triumph hurdle the run before that. So clearly a useful horse when things drop right for her. With the jockey taking off 5lbs. She should be in the shake up here.
LISNAGER FORTUNE looks the stable's main hope on jockey bookings and should appreciate the longer trip: one to consider in this company.

Triumphed in a chase at Navan last March. Recently secured a respectable 3rd place out of 14 in a handicap chase at Navan 41 days ago. With a valuable 7lb claim from the jockey, an each-way bet at 25/1 presents excellent value for this distance winner.

Ideally, he wants softer ground but sits on a nice enough mark to have a wager. He's 4 lbs below his British handicap mark. He ran a bit of a shocker on handicap debut over at Ayr, finishing a well-beaten 5th. To be fair, he was running over the minimum trip. He clearly wants further. He had previously run a nice race at this venue on his penultimate run, finishing 2nd behind Springt De La Mare, beaten 3L by the winner. This hinted that a step up in trip is what he needs. He gets that this time. He's a 3M P2P winner, so this middle-distance trip should be within range. He's only had 4 chase runs and 1 handicap run, so still unexposed. He won his sole bumper run over a similar trip to this. If he runs his race, he should be thereabouts in this competitive heat.

We've seen our fair share of outsiders winning/hitting the Frame this week & at current 33/1 odds (& 5 places on offer) I'm happy to take a swing with Thomas Gibney's 9 year old Gelding LISTENTILLITELLYEA who drops 1lb for finishing 3rd 12 days ago @Fairyhouse (17f Soft/Heavy) & had PATH D'OROUX in behind prior to this was a good run @Down Royal (20f Good) where he looked to be throwing down a challenge behind winner LIGHTKEEPER before falling 1 from the lollypop, the winner went on to win by 7 lengths then won again @Wexford by 8 lengths. Jockey Gavin Brouder remains in the plate & arrives here in decent form with 2 wins/2 places (from 13 runs) the past 30 days. Trainer Thomas Gibney has a 33.33% place strike rate here in County Kildare the past year. This is certainly not an easy task but I've seen much worse 33/1 shots & running off the bottom of the weights I couldn't totally dismiss this charge each way.

SEA MUSIC with his sound sire represents a leading trainer and having been lightly-raced through the main jumps season he could be interesting from his current chase mark. Not highly-tried through his career to date and still with scope in this sphere he appeals.
